subject: MosaicFin onboarding: shortlist + sizing for production
messages:
From: Alexandra Perez <aperez@mosaicfin.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Jul 2028 09:13:00 -0700
Subject: MosaicFin onboarding: shortlist + sizing for production

Hi Sofia / Redwood team,

Thanks for the kickoff yesterday. I'm sending over a short summary of what MosaicFin expects for the initial production rollout so we can lock the model shortlist and sizing during the handoff next week. High-level requirements:

- Use cases: 1) account summarization for customer support (chat-style, multi-turn), 2) structured extraction from transaction notes (single-turn), 3) semantic search over 24 months of customer activity.
- Avg daily active users: ~2,300 (expected to ramp to 8k over 3 months)
- Expected daily requests initially: 35k (mostly extraction + summarization), ramp to 120k/day.
- Typical prompt size: 220 tokens input; summaries target ~380 tokens output. Search embeddings calls: 1.2M/week (batch offline + live scoring).
- Latency requirement: 95th <= 400ms for short extracts; 95th <= 1.2s for multi-turn summaries.

Attached: mosaicfin_token_profile.xlsx (token distribution by endpoint) and a short artifact from their infra team.

Can someone from solutions engineering propose a 2–3 model shortlist with context-length recommendations and rough GPU sizing (peak concurrent RPS target)? Also include fallback model tiers in case we need cost-lower options.

Appreciate it,
Alexandra
Product Ops – MosaicFin

- Prioritize a main model that meets 8k context for mult-turn account summaries; consider a 32k variant only for batched deep-history queries.
- For embeddings: we should separate offline indexing (batch) from low-latency live scoring and size accordingly.

Sofia

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 26 Jul 2028 08:36:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MosaicFin onboarding: shortlist + sizing for production

Hey all — SE write-up below (keeps the shortlist to three tiers with fallback). I included estimated vCPU/GPU footprint for Dedicated sizing and rough hosted cost delta. These are conservative numbers until we run a short benchmarking pass with their sample payloads.

MODEL SHORTLIST (recommended order):
1) Redwood-13B-chat-8k (quantized) — Primary
   - Why: strong mult-turn consistency for summarization, low latency on A100x or H100 with tiled KV cache, good cost/throughput profile.
   - Context: native 8k; acceptable for most account summaries if we micro-chunk long histories.
   - Expected perf: ~80–120 tokens/sec per GPU at median; 95th token latency meets 400ms for 400-token outputs on Dedicated with batching disabled for short calls.

2) Llama-3-Chat-13B-32k (quantized) — Variant for deep-history queries
   - Why: 32k context for single-shot deep-history summaries and long-document extraction. Higher memory, higher per-token cost.
   - Usage pattern: ~10% of requests (scheduled bulk summarization + occasional live deep-dive).

3) OpenFalcon-40B-instruct (8k) — Quality-first fallback
   - Why: higher quality for complex extraction and reasoning; more expensive but useful for highest-value flows. Good for canary/edge cases.

EMBEDDINGS
- Recommendation: Redwood-embed-small for live scoring (low-cost, low-latency). Use Redwood-embed-large offline for high-quality vectorization when running re-index jobs (overnight).

SIZING ESTIMATES (initial -> steady ramp):
- Initial daily request mix: 35k/day => Peak concurrent RPS estimate: 55 RPS (US region peak hour 20% of traffic).
- Target SLOs: 95th latency targets as Alex listed.
- Dedicated capacity (conservative reserve):
   * Primary (Redwood-13B-chat-8k): 4 x A100-80GB (or H100 equiv) to cover peak with headroom (80–100 RPS sustained if batching used).
   * 32k variant: 1 x A100-80GB (on-demand or reserved burst).
   * Embeddings live: 2 x T4 or 1 x A10 for scoring with autoscale.
- Hosted API equivalent: expect 30–40% higher unit cost vs Dedicated but lower ops overhead.

COST NOTES
- Expected per-million token delta between primary and fallback is ~20–35% depending on quantization.

MUTUAL ACTION ITEMS (draft):
- Redwood runs a 2-day benchmark (we need 48 hours of representative payloads + 50 sample long-history summaries).
- MosaicFin to provide anonymized sample payloads and a subset of 150 long-history accounts. (Alex to confirm by Thu EOD)
- SE to deliver a bench report + recommendation by July 29.
- CS to schedule kickoff w/ infra for production network egress + VPC peering details.

I'll attach a quick model comparison PDF and a rough sizing spreadsheet.

Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: MosaicFin onboarding: shortlist + sizing for production

Alexandra — quick follow-up on token math and an ops checklist.

Token / cost worked example (initial):
- Average request = 220 in + 380 out = 600 tokens per request.
- 35k/day -> 21M tokens/day -> ~630M tokens/month (approx).
- If 80% of traffic uses primary model (Redwood-13B-chat-8k) and 20% fallback: project blended cost on hosted API ~ X (detailed numbers in attached spreadsheet).

Ops checklist for Friday handoff:
- Provide sample payloads + 150 long-history accounts (anonymized) -> due Thu EOD (Alex).
- Confirm embedding throughput SLAs and whether live scoring must be <120ms P95.
- Confirm retention/audit requirements for requests (30/90/365 days).
- Decide on Dedicated vs Hosted for month 1 (we recommend Dedicated reserve if predictable throughput is required).

Kimberly
Product Manager, Redwood Console

From: Alexandra Perez <aperez@mosaicfin.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 27 Jul 2028 15:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MosaicFin onboarding: shortlist + sizing for production

Thanks, Ben & Kim — this looks great. We will:
- Share anonymized samples + the 150 long-history accounts by Thu EOD.
- Target live embedding P95 <= 120ms; if that requires Dedicated embed capacity we want that noted as a conditional.
- Retention: 90 days for request traces, 365 days for audit logs (security team requirement).

We agree to the bench run and SE report by July 29. Please include a short section in the report that shows how prefix/KV caching will reduce costs for repeated account summaries.

Also: can you add a brief line about safe-fallback behavior (if primary model fails, route to lower-cost model with a degraded-quality tag)? We need that for our risk register.

Best,
Alexandra
Product Ops – MosaicFin

Alexandra — thanks for the quick turnaround. Confirming next steps and timeline from Redwood side before Friday handoff:

1) SE bench run: Jul 27–29 (Ben) -> report Jul 29 by 5pm PT (deliverable: model perf numbers, P95 latencies, cost per 1M tokens, cache hit assumptions).
2) CS/PM (Sofia/Kim/Marissa): Friday handoff meeting Jul 31 at 09:00 PT. Agenda: model selection decision, Dedicated vs Hosted recommendation, embedding SLA confirmation, mutual action plan sign-off.
3) Legal/procurement: initiate onboarding PO & SOW draft (Marissa will loop in finance).
4) Ops: confirm VPC/egress requirements and audit log retention (90/365) -> infra contact to be added during handoff.

Safe-fallback behavior: we'll include a routing policy that tags responses as "degraded_output" when falling back and emits a trace event for audit. We'll also include a configurable rate threshold to trigger fallback.

Thanks — looking forward to the handoff.

Marissa Cole
Program Lead, Customer Success, Redwood Inference
